articles.title: The quiet economics of a library that never closes
articles.author: Maren Holt
articles.hook: A city kept one branch open all night and counted who came. Shift workers, students and insomniacs, mostly. Holt argues the cost per visit beat every daytime branch.

articles.title: Why your build is slow, told by the cache
articles.author: Tomas Ilves
articles.hook: Most slow builds are cache misses nobody looked at. Ilves walks one repo from 14 minutes to 90 seconds by reading the miss log, with no new tools.

articles.title: A field guide to the bees on your balcony
articles.author: Asha Rao
articles.hook: Twelve species turn up on an ordinary city balcony in a summer. Rao shows how to tell them apart with a phone and patience, and which plants keep them coming.

articles.title: Notes from a year of writing by hand
articles.author: Jun Park
articles.hook: Park drafted everything on paper for a year. Fewer words, fewer rewrites, and a habit of deciding before typing. The cost was search, which he solved with an index card box.

articles.title: What a lighthouse keeper's log teaches about on-call
articles.author: Ines Moreau
articles.hook: Nineteenth-century keepers logged weather, oil and visitors every four hours. Moreau reads three logs as incident reports and finds the same handoff mistakes teams make today.

articles.title: The case for boring maps
articles.author: Lena Fischer
articles.hook: Fischer compares two transit maps of one city. The plain one wins on every rider test, and she explains why decoration costs more than it looks.
